paragraphs.title: The Famine and the Promise to Remain in the Land

easy.question: What was in the land at the beginning of the passage?
easy.explanation: The first verse says, “And there was a famine in the land.”

easy.question: Where did Isaac go?
easy.explanation: Isaac went to Gerar, to Abimelech king of the Philistines.

easy.question: What did the Lord command Isaac?
answers: Not to go down to Egypt
easy.explanation: The Lord told Isaac, “Go not down into Egypt.”

medium.question: What happened after the famine came to the land?
answers: Isaac went to Gerar, and the Lord appeared to him
Isaac immediately went down to Egypt
medium.explanation: Because of the famine, Isaac went to Gerar, where the Lord appeared to him.

medium.question: Why did the Lord mention Abraham in His words to Isaac?
answers: Because Abraham was king of the Philistines
Because the Lord was keeping the oath He swore to Abraham
Because Abraham had gone down to Egypt
medium.explanation: The Lord promised to give Isaac the land and to perform the oath He had sworn to Abraham.

medium.question: What does “Sojourn in this land” mean in context?
answers: Live in the land for a time
medium.explanation: The command appears with the instruction not to go to Egypt, so it means to remain and live in the land.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the repetition of “unto thy seed” in verses 3–4?
answers: The blessing is also intended for Isaac’s descendants
The blessing is intended only for Abraham
The blessing is intended only for the king of the Philistines
challenge.explanation: The Lord promises land, multiplication, and blessing both to Isaac and to his descendants.

challenge.question: What is the meaning of the promise “in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed”?
answers: All the nations will leave the land
Isaac’s descendants will be a source of blessing to the nations
All the nations will become kings
challenge.explanation: The verse teaches that the nations will receive blessing through Isaac’s descendants.

challenge.question: What detail about the famine is easy to miss in the first verse?
answers: The famine was only in Egypt
The famine occurred after Isaac’s death
There was another famine besides the one in Abraham’s days
challenge.explanation: The phrase “beside the first famine” shows that this was a separate famine from the one in Abraham’s days.

questions.question: What can we infer from the repetition of “unto thy seed” in verses 3–4?
answers: The blessing is also intended for Isaac’s descendants
The blessing is intended only for Abraham
The blessing is intended only for the king of the Philistines
questions.explanation: The Lord promises land, multiplication, and blessing both to Isaac and to his descendants.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the promise “in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed”?
answers: All the nations will leave the land
Isaac’s descendants will be a source of blessing to the nations
All the nations will become kings
questions.explanation: The verse teaches that the nations will receive blessing through Isaac’s descendants.

answers: The famine was only in Egypt
The famine occurred after Isaac’s death
There was another famine besides the one in Abraham’s days
questions.explanation: The phrase “beside the first famine” shows that this was a separate famine from the one in Abraham’s days.

easy.question: Where did Isaac settle?
easy.explanation: Verse 6 says, “And Isaac dwelt in Gerar.”

easy.question: Who was Isaac’s wife?
easy.explanation: Verse 8 explicitly says that Isaac was sporting with Rebekah his wife.

easy.question: Why did Isaac say that Rebekah was his sister?
answers: Because he did not know her
Because he feared they would kill him because of her
easy.explanation: Isaac said he feared that the men of the place would kill him for Rebekah.

medium.question: What caused Abimelech to realize that Rebekah was Isaac’s wife?
answers: He saw Isaac sporting with Rebekah from a window
The men of the place told him
medium.explanation: After Isaac had been there a long time, Abimelech looked out a window and saw Isaac with Rebekah.

medium.question: What does “when he had been there a long time” mean?
answers: Isaac remained there for a long time
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates that Isaac had stayed in Gerar for a considerable time.

medium.question: What did Abimelech do after realizing that Rebekah was Isaac’s wife?
answers: He sent Isaac out of the land
He took Rebekah into his house
He commanded that anyone who touched Isaac or Rebekah be put to death
medium.explanation: Abimelech warned all his people and declared the death penalty for anyone who harmed Isaac or Rebekah.

challenge.question: What can we understand from Abimelech’s words, “thou shouldest have brought guiltiness upon us”?
answers: The act could have brought guilt upon all the people
He wanted to punish only Rebekah
challenge.explanation: Abimelech said that if one of his people had lain with Rebekah, guilt would have come upon the entire people.

challenge.question: How did seeing Isaac “sporting with Rebekah his wife” help Abimelech understand the truth?
answers: It showed that Rebekah was Isaac’s sister
Their behavior showed that they were a couple, not siblings
It proved that Rebekah was queen of the Philistines
challenge.explanation: The close behavior Abimelech saw did not fit Isaac’s claim that Rebekah was his sister, so he understood that she was his wife.

challenge.question: What was the main difference between Isaac’s fear and Abimelech’s response?
answers: Isaac feared famine, while Abimelech feared war
Isaac feared Rebekah would leave, while Abimelech wanted to banish her
Isaac feared they would kill him, while Abimelech protected them both by decree
challenge.explanation: Isaac hid his marriage because he feared for his life, while Abimelech later commanded that Isaac and Rebekah be protected.

questions.question: What can we understand from Abimelech’s words, “thou shouldest have brought guiltiness upon us”?
answers: The act could have brought guilt upon all the people
He wanted to punish only Rebekah
questions.explanation: Abimelech said that if one of his people had lain with Rebekah, guilt would have come upon the entire people.

questions.question: How did seeing Isaac “sporting with Rebekah his wife” help Abimelech understand the truth?
answers: It showed that Rebekah was Isaac’s sister
Their behavior showed that they were a couple, not siblings
It proved that Rebekah was queen of the Philistines
questions.explanation: The close behavior Abimelech saw did not fit Isaac’s claim that Rebekah was his sister, so he understood that she was his wife.

questions.question: What was the main difference between Isaac’s fear and Abimelech’s response?
answers: Isaac feared famine, while Abimelech feared war
Isaac feared Rebekah would leave, while Abimelech wanted to banish her
Isaac feared they would kill him, while Abimelech protected them both by decree
questions.explanation: Isaac hid his marriage because he feared for his life, while Abimelech later commanded that Isaac and Rebekah be protected.

easy.question: What did Isaac sow in that land?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Then Isaac sowed in that land.”

easy.question: Who envied Isaac?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the Philistines envied him.”

easy.question: Why did Abimelech ask Isaac to leave?
answers: Because Isaac had become much mightier than they
easy.explanation: Abimelech told Isaac, “thou art much mightier than we.”

medium.question: According to the order of the verses, what caused the Philistines to envy Isaac?
answers: Isaac became wealthy and very powerful
medium.explanation: Isaac prospered, had flocks, herds, and many servants, so the Philistines envied him.

medium.question: What does “possession” mean in “possession of flocks” and “possession of herds”?
medium.explanation: The context mentions flocks and herds, so “possession” refers to livestock Isaac owned.

medium.question: What did the Philistines do to the wells Abraham’s servants had dug?
answers: They stopped them and filled them with earth
medium.explanation: The verse says that they stopped the wells and filled them with earth.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that Abimelech wanted Isaac to leave?
answers: Isaac’s power and wealth had become a threat to the local people
Abimelech wanted to give Isaac new wells
challenge.explanation: Abimelech said that Isaac had become much mightier than they, so he asked Isaac to move away.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “went forward, and grew” emphasize?
answers: Isaac continued to grow and prosper
Isaac moved from place to place
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes an ongoing process of growth and success.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the Philistines harmed Abraham’s legacy, not only Isaac’s property?
answers: They stopped wells dug by Abraham’s servants
challenge.explanation: The wells had been dug by Abraham’s servants, so stopping them also harmed the family’s legacy.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that Abimelech wanted Isaac to leave?
answers: Isaac’s power and wealth had become a threat to the local people
Abimelech wanted to give Isaac new wells
questions.explanation: Abimelech said that Isaac had become much mightier than they, so he asked Isaac to move away.

questions.question: What does the phrase “went forward, and grew” emphasize?
answers: Isaac continued to grow and prosper
Isaac moved from place to place
questions.explanation: The wording emphasizes an ongoing process of growth and success.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the Philistines harmed Abraham’s legacy, not only Isaac’s property?
answers: They stopped wells dug by Abraham’s servants
questions.explanation: The wells had been dug by Abraham’s servants, so stopping them also harmed the family’s legacy.

paragraphs.title: Reopening the Old Wells and Digging New Ones

easy.question: What did Isaac do in the valley of Gerar?
answers: He pitched his tent and settled there
easy.explanation: The verse says that Isaac pitched his tent in the valley of Gerar and dwelt there.

easy.question: Who had dug the wells that Isaac dug again?
easy.explanation: They were the wells Abraham’s servants had dug in Abraham’s days.

easy.question: What name did Isaac give the well that was not disputed?
easy.explanation: Isaac called the third well, over which they did not strive, Rehoboth.

medium.question: Why did Isaac dig Abraham’s wells again?
answers: The Philistines had stopped them after Abraham’s death
The herdsmen of Gerar asked him to
medium.explanation: Because the Philistines had stopped the wells, Isaac reopened them.

medium.question: What happened after the herdsmen of Gerar strove with Isaac’s herdsmen over the first well?
answers: Isaac’s servants dug another well, and they strove over that one too
Isaac returned to his father’s house
medium.explanation: After the dispute over Esek, they dug another well, but a dispute arose over that one as well.

medium.question: What does “he removed from thence” mean?
medium.explanation: The context shows that Isaac left the place and dug another well elsewhere.

challenge.question: What does the change from the names Esek and Sitnah to Rehoboth teach?
answers: Isaac moved from conflict to a place of peace and room
The herdsmen of Gerar became the well owners
challenge.explanation: The first names describe disputes, while the final name describes a place where there was room and no dispute.

challenge.question: Why did Isaac retain the names his father had given the wells?
answers: To preserve his connection to Abraham’s legacy
To name them after the herdsmen of Gerar
challenge.explanation: Keeping the names expresses continuity with Abraham’s work and legacy.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the phrase “a well of springing water”?
answers: The well contained flowing or fresh water
challenge.explanation: “Springing water” refers to fresh or naturally flowing water.

questions.question: What does the change from the names Esek and Sitnah to Rehoboth teach?
answers: Isaac moved from conflict to a place of peace and room
The herdsmen of Gerar became the well owners
questions.explanation: The first names describe disputes, while the final name describes a place where there was room and no dispute.

questions.question: Why did Isaac retain the names his father had given the wells?
answers: To preserve his connection to Abraham’s legacy
To name them after the herdsmen of Gerar
questions.explanation: Keeping the names expresses continuity with Abraham’s work and legacy.

questions.question: What can we understand from the phrase “a well of springing water”?
answers: The well contained flowing or fresh water
questions.explanation: “Springing water” refers to fresh or naturally flowing water.

paragraphs.title: Beersheba and the Lord’s Appearance at Night

easy.question: Where did Isaac go in verse 23?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And he went up from thence to Beersheba.”

easy.question: Who appeared to Isaac at night?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And the Lord appeared unto him.”

easy.question: What did Isaac build there?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And he builded an altar there.”

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Isaac arrived at Beersheba, the Lord appeared to him, and then Isaac built an altar
Isaac built an altar, then the Lord appeared to him, and then he arrived at Beersheba
Isaac’s servants dug a well, and then Isaac went to Gerar
medium.explanation: First Isaac went to Beersheba, then the Lord appeared to him, and afterward Isaac built an altar.

medium.question: Why did the Lord promise Isaac blessing and many descendants?
answers: Because Isaac was afraid at night
medium.explanation: The Lord said, “I will bless thee, and multiply thy seed for my servant Abraham’s sake.”

medium.question: What does “for my servant Abraham’s sake” mean?
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the Lord would multiply Isaac’s descendants because of Abraham.

challenge.question: What fear of Isaac is implied by the Lord’s words, “Fear not”?
answers: Isaac feared he would have no well
Isaac feared Abraham would be angry with him
challenge.explanation: The command “Fear not” shows that Isaac needed encouragement because of fear or danger.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Isaac’s actions after the Lord appeared to him?
answers: He established his life and worship there: he built an altar, called on the Lord, and pitched his tent
He sent his servants to look for Abraham
challenge.explanation: Building the altar, calling on the Lord, and pitching his tent show that Isaac settled there and accepted the Lord’s promise.

challenge.question: What does the repetition of “there” in verse 25 emphasize?
answers: Isaac’s servants did not know where they were
Beersheba became central to Isaac’s life and work
challenge.explanation: The repeated location connects the altar, tent, and well with the same important place.

questions.question: What fear of Isaac is implied by the Lord’s words, “Fear not”?
answers: Isaac feared he would have no well
Isaac feared Abraham would be angry with him
questions.explanation: The command “Fear not” shows that Isaac needed encouragement because of fear or danger.

questions.question: What can we infer from Isaac’s actions after the Lord appeared to him?
answers: He established his life and worship there: he built an altar, called on the Lord, and pitched his tent
He sent his servants to look for Abraham
questions.explanation: Building the altar, calling on the Lord, and pitching his tent show that Isaac settled there and accepted the Lord’s promise.

questions.question: What does the repetition of “there” in verse 25 emphasize?
answers: Isaac’s servants did not know where they were
Beersheba became central to Isaac’s life and work
questions.explanation: The repeated location connects the altar, tent, and well with the same important place.

paragraphs.title: Abimelech Seeks a Covenant of Peace

easy.question: Who came to Isaac from Gerar?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Abimelech went to Isaac from Gerar.

easy.question: What did Isaac ask Abimelech and his men?
answers: Why did you leave the land?
Why have you come to me?
Why did you take my possessions?
easy.explanation: Isaac asked them, “Wherefore come ye to me?” because they had hated him and sent him away.

easy.question: What did Abimelech and his men want to make with Isaac?
easy.explanation: They asked for an oath and a covenant with Isaac.

medium.question: Why did Abimelech and his men want to make a covenant with Isaac?
answers: They wanted to take his wells
They saw that the Lord was with him
Isaac had asked them for money
medium.explanation: They said, “We saw certainly that the Lord was with thee,” and therefore sought peace and a covenant.

medium.question: What does “an oath betwixt us” mean?
medium.explanation: In the context of making a covenant, an oath is a solemn promise between the parties.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events?
answers: Isaac blessed Abimelech, and then Abimelech came to him
Abimelech and his men came, Isaac questioned them, and they proposed a covenant
Abimelech attacked Isaac, and then Isaac left
medium.explanation: First Abimelech and his men came, then Isaac asked why they had come, and finally they proposed a covenant.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Abimelech’s coming with Ahuzzath and Phichol?
answers: He came to seek work from Isaac
The meeting was official and politically important
challenge.explanation: The presence of a friend and army commander suggests an official delegation to arrange relations and a covenant.

challenge.question: What caused Abimelech and his men to change their attitude toward Isaac?
answers: They recognized that the Lord blessed and accompanied Isaac
Isaac promised to leave the land immediately
They discovered that Isaac was weaker than they were
challenge.explanation: Although they had previously sent Isaac away, they now acknowledged that the Lord was with him and sought peace.

challenge.question: What special meaning do their words “we have sent thee away in peace” have?
answers: They claimed never to have met Isaac
They presented Isaac’s expulsion as an act not intended to harm him
They asked Isaac to go to war
challenge.explanation: They emphasized that, in their view, they had sent Isaac away peacefully and had done him no harm, supporting their request for a covenant.

questions.question: What can we infer from Abimelech’s coming with Ahuzzath and Phichol?
answers: He came to seek work from Isaac
The meeting was official and politically important
questions.explanation: The presence of a friend and army commander suggests an official delegation to arrange relations and a covenant.

questions.question: What caused Abimelech and his men to change their attitude toward Isaac?
answers: They recognized that the Lord blessed and accompanied Isaac
Isaac promised to leave the land immediately
They discovered that Isaac was weaker than they were
questions.explanation: Although they had previously sent Isaac away, they now acknowledged that the Lord was with him and sought peace.

questions.question: What special meaning do their words “we have sent thee away in peace” have?
answers: They claimed never to have met Isaac
They presented Isaac’s expulsion as an act not intended to harm him
They asked Isaac to go to war
questions.explanation: They emphasized that, in their view, they had sent Isaac away peacefully and had done him no harm, supporting their request for a covenant.

easy.question: What did Isaac do for them?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And he made them a feast.”

easy.question: What did the people do at the feast?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “and they did eat and drink.”

easy.question: What appears in the verse after the feast was made?
easy.explanation: After the feast was made, the verse describes them eating and drinking.

medium.question: What was the order of events in the verse?
answers: They made a feast, and afterward they ate and drank
They drank, then ate, and then made a feast
They ate, then made a feast, and then drank
medium.explanation: The verse first describes making the feast and then describes eating and drinking.

medium.question: What does “feast” mean in “he made them a feast”?
medium.explanation: Since the verse immediately mentions eating and drinking, it refers to a special meal or festive hospitality.

medium.question: Who do “them” and “they did eat” refer to?
answers: Only the person who prepared the feast
The people who were guests at the feast
medium.explanation: The plural pronouns refer to the people for whom the feast was prepared and who ate and drank.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the plural verbs “they did eat and drink”?
answers: Only one person ate and drank
Several people participated in eating and drinking
challenge.explanation: The plural verbs describe the participation of several people.

challenge.question: What is the most accurate description of the host and guests in the verse?
answers: The host prepared a meal, and the guests took part in it
The guests prepared the meal, and the host only watched
Everyone left before the meal began
challenge.explanation: “He made them” describes the host’s action, while “they did eat and drink” describes the guests’ participation.

challenge.question: What does the appearance of both “eat” and “drink” emphasize?
answers: The feast involved only preparing food
The participants enjoyed a meal with both food and drink
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly mentions both eating and drinking, describing a complete meal.

questions.question: What can we infer from the plural verbs “they did eat and drink”?
answers: Only one person ate and drank
Several people participated in eating and drinking
questions.explanation: The plural verbs describe the participation of several people.

questions.question: What is the most accurate description of the host and guests in the verse?
answers: The host prepared a meal, and the guests took part in it
The guests prepared the meal, and the host only watched
Everyone left before the meal began
questions.explanation: “He made them” describes the host’s action, while “they did eat and drink” describes the guests’ participation.

questions.question: What does the appearance of both “eat” and “drink” emphasize?
answers: The feast involved only preparing food
The participants enjoyed a meal with both food and drink
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly mentions both eating and drinking, describing a complete meal.

paragraphs.title: A Covenant of Peace between Isaac and Abimelech

easy.question: When did Isaac and the men of Gerar swear to one another?
easy.explanation: The verse says they rose early in the morning and then swore to one another.

easy.question: What did Isaac do after they swore to one another?
answers: He invited them into his house
He stayed with them in the city
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And Isaac sent them away.”

easy.question: How did the men of Gerar leave Isaac?
easy.explanation: The verse ends by saying, “they departed from him in peace.”

medium.question: What happened before the men of Gerar left Isaac?
medium.explanation: First they swore to one another; afterward Isaac sent them away.

medium.question: What does “Isaac sent them away” mean?
answers: He sent them away from him
medium.explanation: It means Isaac allowed them to leave; the following phrase says they departed from him.

medium.question: What was the connection between the oath and the peaceful ending?
answers: The oath caused them to remain with Isaac
The oath caused them to go to war
The oath expressed an agreement that allowed them to part peacefully
medium.explanation: After swearing to one another, they separated from Isaac without conflict.

challenge.question: What does “one to another” show about the oath?
answers: Only one of the men of Gerar swore
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that each party swore to the other, making it a mutual oath.

challenge.question: What does “from him” refer to in “they departed from him”?
answers: The place to which Isaac sent them
challenge.explanation: It means that the men of Gerar moved away from Isaac and his place.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the sequence—rising, swearing, sending, and departing in peace?
answers: The meeting ended without a decision
Agreement was reached and the dispute ended in a quiet separation
challenge.explanation: The sequence shows that after the oath, Isaac sent them away and they left peacefully.

questions.question: What does “one to another” show about the oath?
answers: Only one of the men of Gerar swore
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that each party swore to the other, making it a mutual oath.

questions.question: What does “from him” refer to in “they departed from him”?
answers: The place to which Isaac sent them
questions.explanation: It means that the men of Gerar moved away from Isaac and his place.

questions.question: What can we infer from the sequence—rising, swearing, sending, and departing in peace?
answers: The meeting ended without a decision
Agreement was reached and the dispute ended in a quiet separation
questions.explanation: The sequence shows that after the oath, Isaac sent them away and they left peacefully.

easy.question: Who came to Isaac?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Isaac’s servants came to him.

easy.question: What did Isaac’s servants tell him about?
easy.explanation: They told Isaac about the well they had dug.

easy.question: What did Isaac’s servants find?
easy.explanation: They said to Isaac, “We have found water.”

medium.question: What did Isaac’s servants do before finding water?
medium.explanation: They dug a well, and afterward found water in it.

medium.question: What does “concerning” mean in “they told him concerning the well”?
medium.explanation: It means “about” or “regarding”; the servants told Isaac about the well.

medium.question: What did Isaac do after hearing that they had found water?
answers: He gave the well a name
medium.explanation: After hearing the news, Isaac named the well Shebah.

challenge.question: Which sequence correctly describes the verses?
answers: Isaac named the well, and then the servants dug it
The servants found water, and then Isaac left the city
The servants dug a well, found water, and Isaac named it
challenge.explanation: First the well was dug, then water was found, and finally Isaac named it Shebah.

challenge.question: What is the connection between the name “Shebah” and the city’s name, Beersheba?
answers: The city was named after the well’s name
The well was named after the city
challenge.explanation: The verse says, “therefore the name of the city is Beersheba,” connecting the city’s name with the well.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the words “unto this day”?
answers: The name continued to be used later
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the name Beersheba remained in use after the events described.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes the verses?
answers: Isaac named the well, and then the servants dug it
The servants found water, and then Isaac left the city
The servants dug a well, found water, and Isaac named it
questions.explanation: First the well was dug, then water was found, and finally Isaac named it Shebah.

questions.question: What is the connection between the name “Shebah” and the city’s name, Beersheba?
answers: The city was named after the well’s name
The well was named after the city
questions.explanation: The verse says, “therefore the name of the city is Beersheba,” connecting the city’s name with the well.

questions.question: What can we infer from the words “unto this day”?
answers: The name continued to be used later
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the name Beersheba remained in use after the events described.

paragraphs.title: Esau’s Marriages and the Grief in Isaac and Rebekah’s Household

easy.question: How old was Esau when he took wives?
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says that Esau was forty years old.

easy.question: How many wives did Esau take?
easy.explanation: Esau took Judith and Bashemath, two wives.

easy.question: To whom were the wives a grief of mind?
easy.explanation: The verse says that they were a grief of mind to Isaac and Rebekah.

medium.question: What can we understand from the verse mentioning Esau’s age before describing his marriages?
answers: He was already an adult when he married
He was born at that time
medium.explanation: Mentioning that he was forty shows that Esau was an adult when he took wives.

medium.question: What does “a grief of mind” mean in this context?
medium.explanation: The phrase describes something that caused Isaac and Rebekah sorrow and distress.

medium.question: What was the relationship between Esau’s marriages and Isaac and Rebekah’s response?
answers: Esau’s marriages had no effect on them
medium.explanation: Immediately after describing the marriages, the verse says that the wives were a grief of mind to Isaac and Rebekah.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that both of Esau’s wives are called Hittites?
answers: Both belonged to the Hittite people
challenge.explanation: The designation “Hittite” identifies their origin.

challenge.question: Why is the phrase “which were” appropriate in the verse?
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to Esau’s two wives.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes that the problem was connected to Esau’s wives, not merely to his marrying?
answers: The verse says that the wives were a grief of mind to Isaac and Rebekah
The verse says Esau was forty years old
challenge.explanation: The verse directly attributes the grief to the wives, rather than simply to the fact that Esau married.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that both of Esau’s wives are called Hittites?
answers: Both belonged to the Hittite people
questions.explanation: The designation “Hittite” identifies their origin.

questions.question: Why is the phrase “which were” appropriate in the verse?
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to Esau’s two wives.

questions.question: Which detail emphasizes that the problem was connected to Esau’s wives, not merely to his marrying?
answers: The verse says that the wives were a grief of mind to Isaac and Rebekah
The verse says Esau was forty years old
questions.explanation: The verse directly attributes the grief to the wives, rather than simply to the fact that Esau married.
